name: Arthur Smith

views.text: A punishing run game and play-action can revive a quarterback's career.
Going from head coach back to coordinator is easy if you have no ego about it.
Structure and accountability come first when taking over a struggling offense.
You earn your way up from the bottom of a staff; a family name buys nothing.
Sitting out a season is not an option for someone who wants to compete.
A team that runs up the score late will hear about it.

signatures: talks about the grind of the job as something he loves
credits the people who mentored him on the way up from quality control
deflects talk of his famous family toward his own work
want: to show that his Tennessee offense was no fluke and earn another shot at running a team
fear: that his three losing seasons in Atlanta become the summary of his career
voice: Intense, competitive and blunt, with a dry sense of humor about how few people in coaching are well-adjusted. He talks about structure, accountability and the grind, credits mentors and stays humble about his background. His temper can show after a lopsided loss.

evidence.summary: Profile at his Falcons hiring: humble about his family's wealth, driven and competitive, loved practice and the grind; worked up from analyst and quality control; as Titans coordinator revitalized Tannehill and Henry; close to his family and left Washington to advance on his own merit.

Atlanta fires him after a third straight 7-10 season; after a 48-17 finale he confronted Saints coach Dennis Allen with profane language over late scoring; notes criticism of how he used Robinson, Pitts and London. News write-up.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), via Yahoo Sports
evidence.summary: Tomlin explains hiring him: head-coaching experience helps Tomlin see subtle things, and he wants to trade ideas on broader topics; Smith's job is fixing a weak 2023 offense. Shows the working relationship.

He says he jumped at Tomlin's call while on vacation after his firing, sees the job as a chance to learn, says stepping back to coordinator is easy without ego, has brought structure and accountability, and wants to compete. His own words.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), Darin Gantt
evidence.summary: Newly promoted in Tennessee, he calls himself lucky and proud of his father, credits him with teaching humility and self-made success, and says he has much work left. His words.
